metaDescription: Re-indent TypeScript or JavaScript by brace depth, fix blank lines and break minified code into lines. Strings, templates and regexes stay intact.
intro: Fixes indentation, blank lines and optionally line breaks in TypeScript code without sending it anywhere.
why:
Messy indentation hides the structure of TypeScript code, and minified or copy-pasted code is worse. A re-indenter gives you the block layout back quickly.

The tool reads your code with a small scanner that knows strings, comments and raw literals, so braces inside them are ignored. It then sets the indent from bracket depth and, if you ask, puts a line break after braces and semicolons. It is not Prettier.
howTo: Pick the indent and whether to break lines at braces and semicolons.
Run Prettier locally if you need exact style.

faq.q: Is this the same as Prettier?
faq.a: No. Prettier also rewrites spacing, quotes and wraps lines to a print width. This tool re-indents and optionally breaks lines only.

faq.q: Will it change what my code does?
faq.a: It only changes whitespace outside strings, comments and raw literals. Test results: the non-whitespace text was unchanged on all test files, and re-running the tool gave the same output. Review the diff anyway.
Wrapping needs a full parser. This tool does not have one.
No. Everything runs in your browser and nothing is uploaded.
